title: Set 158

sentences.ko: 회사를 그만둘까 말까 계속 왔다 갔다 해. 그러니까, 월급은 괜찮은데 월요일이 너무 싫어서 일요일 오후만 되면 벌써 우울해지거든. 이거 정상 아니잖아, 그치?
sentences.text: I keep going back and forth on quitting. Like, the pay's fine, but I dread Monday so much that I'm already miserable by Sunday afternoon, and I don't think that's normal, is it?

alts.text: Still can't decide if I should quit. The money's fine, but I dread Mondays so bad I'm already miserable by Sunday afternoon. That's not normal, right?

I continue to go back and forth on whether to resign. The salary is adequate, but I dread Mondays so much that I am already unhappy by Sunday afternoon, and I do not believe that is normal. Would you agree?

sentences.note: **go back and forth on** 은 어떤 일을 두고 마음이 이랬다저랬다 한다는 뜻입니다. **dread** 는 다가올 일이 끔찍하게 싫고 두렵다는 말이에요.

sentences.ko: 나 달리기 시작한다고 했던 거 기억나? 응, 운동화에 시계까지 다 샀는데, 해가 일찍 지기 시작하니까 그 뒤로 한 번도 안 나갔어. 그래서 지금은 마트 걸어갈 때 신는 엄청 좋은 운동화가 생겼지.
sentences.text: Remember when I said I was getting into running? Yeah, I bought the shoes and the watch and everything, and then it got dark early and I just never went back out. So now I've got really nice shoes for walking to the store.

alts.text: You know how I was gonna get into running? I got the shoes, the watch, all of it, then it started getting dark early and I never went out again. So now I've got super nice shoes for walking to the store.

Do you recall when I mentioned that I was taking up running? I purchased the shoes, the watch, and everything else, but then it began to get dark early and I never went out again. As a result, I now own very good shoes for walking to the store.

sentences.note: **get into** 는 어떤 취미나 활동에 재미를 붙여 시작한다는 뜻입니다. 끝의 **and everything** 은 그 밖의 것까지 전부라는 뜻으로 말할 때 자주 붙여요.

sentences.ko: 훨씬 넓고 발코니도 있는 집을 찾았는데, 출퇴근 운전이 편도로 20분쯤 더 걸리게 돼. 그래서 내가 진짜 그 집이 좋은 건지, 아니면 그냥 지금 아파트가 지겨운 건지 모르겠어.
sentences.text: We found this place that's way bigger and it's got a balcony, but it'd add like twenty minutes to my drive each way, so I can't tell if I actually want it or if I'm just sick of our apartment.

alts.text: So we found a way bigger place with a balcony, but it's like twenty more minutes each way on my drive, and I can't tell if I really want it or I'm just sick of our apartment.

We found a considerably larger place with a balcony, but it would add approximately twenty minutes to my drive in each direction, so I cannot tell whether I genuinely want it or whether I am simply tired of our apartment.

sentences.note: **each way** 는 가는 길과 오는 길 각각, 즉 편도로 따져서라는 뜻입니다. **sick of** 는 무언가에 질렸다, 지겹다는 말이에요.

sentences.ko: 토요일에 바비큐 하기로 했는데, 일기예보에 오후 내내 비가 쏟아진대. 그래서 다들 대신 우리 집으로 오기로 했는데, 나 청소도 아직 안 했어.
sentences.text: We were supposed to do a barbecue on Saturday, but the forecast says it's going to pour all afternoon, so now everybody's coming over to our place instead, and I haven't even cleaned.

alts.text: So the barbecue Saturday? Forecast says it's gonna pour all afternoon, so now everyone's coming to our place instead, and I haven't even cleaned.
We had planned to hold a barbecue on Saturday, but the forecast indicates heavy rain throughout the afternoon, so everyone will now be coming to our home instead, and I have not yet cleaned.

sentences.note: **pour** 는 비가 억수같이 쏟아진다는 뜻입니다. **come over** 는 누군가의 집에 놀러 온다는 말이에요.

sentences.ko: 택배가 월요일에 오기로 돼 있었는데, 배송 조회를 하면 매일 그냥 지연됐다고만 나오고 실제로 어디 있는지는 아무도 말을 못 해 줘. 취소하고 싶은데, 그러면 다른 데서 처음부터 다시 주문해야 하잖아.
sentences.text: My package was supposed to be here Monday, and every day the tracking just says it's delayed, but nobody can tell me where it actually is. I'd cancel it, but then I'd have to order it all over again somewhere else.

alts.text: Ugh, my package should've come Monday. Every day the tracking just says delayed and nobody can tell me where it actually is. I'd cancel, but then I'd have to order it all over again someplace else.

My package was scheduled to arrive on Monday, and each day the tracking information simply states that it has been delayed, yet no one is able to tell me where it actually is. I would cancel the order, but I would then have to place it again with another seller.

sentences.note: **supposed to** 는 원래 그러기로 되어 있었다는 뜻으로, 일이 계획대로 안 됐을 때 많이 씁니다. **all over again** 은 처음부터 다시 한 번이라는 말이에요.

reviewed: 1번 한국어 '이거 정상 아니지, 그렇지?' 는 같은 말을 두 번 물어 어색해서 '이거 정상 아니잖아, 그치?' 로 고침
5번 한국어 '아무도 몰라' 는 영어(nobody can tell me)와 뜻이 달라서 '아무도 말을 못 해 줘' 로 고침
